tara: Quick smoke for Polaris-13B int4 shows generation collapse on instruction summarization. Short replies, repeated hallucinations.
vik: did you use our standard gptq-per-channel recipe? any exporter warnings?
tara: yes gptq-per-channel. Exporter emitted: `WARNING: normalizer mismatch detected (nfkd vs nfc); appended 2 sentinels and remapped ids +2`
rene: nfkd vs nfc mismatch can create duplicate-like tokens. Check tokenizer.encode for special tokens and embedding indices.
tara: small check: `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(["<sep>","<pad>"]) -> [50003,0]` but `embeddings.index_of("<sep>") -> 50005`
vik: that's a +2 offset. That will shift prompt prefixes and KV cache columns. Also verify rotary head permutation: Polaris uses permuted rotary order (head_perm array). If KV columns shifted, rotary freqs applied to wrong heads.
ci-bot: artifact uploaded: gs://redwood-onboard/polaris/1733337777/token-and-rotary-dump.txt :white_check_mark:
tara: after applying manual sentinel remap (-2) and re-running 200-sample smoke, rouge-L recovered to 98% of fp16. But long-context (>2048) still degrades.
rene: sounds like two issues: 1) token-id translation (hotfixable) 2) headwise rotary ordering vs kvcache column indexing for long contexts. Add instrumentation to log kv-column->token-id mapping across time.
vik: also run quant-ablation: per-channel vs per-tensor symmetric; sometimes long-context attention is sensitive to per-tensor quant noise in head-proj matrices.
tara: filing exporter bug: exporters should emit mapping.json and verify normalizer used. (cc @exporter-bot).
exporter-bot: ISSUE created: exporter/normalizer-mismatch-1733337777 (https://issues/redwood/13121)
vik: plan: (tara) hotfix mapping in snapshot & rerun full eval; (rene) add kv+rotary trace tool; (vik) run quick quant ablation on 300 long-context samples. Post results here. :mag:
